solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leading European model developed a simple photographic technique

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
the leading letter is the one at the front of the word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
the Model T, Ford's famous early car
taken as written

explanation.surface: A top European fashion model has come up with an easy photographic trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a fashion model, but it is the Model T car, giving one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-lapse photography takes frames at long intervals, so slow change plays back sped up; it is a camera method.

clue.text: Speed of stream regularly recorded on river

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: How fast a stream flows, logged at intervals on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'recorded on' places the first piece above, so before, the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the rate or pace of music or activity, so it means speed.

clue.text: Heartless tycoon initially threw journalist in shed

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is removed

parts.note: a mogul is a powerful business magnate

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter
ED is short for editor, the standard crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A cruel business boss at first hurled a reporter into an outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a garden hut but is the past tense verb, as a snake sheds its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Moulted means cast off feathers, hair or skin, which is what an animal that has shed its coat did.

clue.text: Kitchen utensil on the counter in Sheffield alehouse

indicators.note: counter means running against the usual direction, so the letters go backwards
the answer sits in the run of letters across the next two words

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the city and the start of the pub

explanation.surface: A serving spoon lies on the bar of a Sheffield pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' invites a bar top or worktop, but it signals reading backwards; Sheffield, a steel city, fits the cutlery picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladle is a long-handled deep spoon for serving soup, a standard kitchen tool.

clue.text: Deviant solver picked up range of knowledge

indicators.note: picking up a signal means hearing it, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: a perv is a sexual deviant, and the solver is addressed as you

explanation.surface: A twisted puzzler overheard something across the whole field of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords call the solver 'you'; said together, the two words sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Purview means the scope or extent of someone's authority or understanding, so it is a range of knowledge.

clue.text: Provide revolutionary satellite with extremely sensitive balance

parts.note: to equip is to provide with what is needed

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Io is one of Jupiter's moons

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Supply a rotating satellite with a very delicate balancing system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests an orbiting satellite, but it signals the moon's name reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipoise is a state of equal balance between forces, a formal word for balance.

clue.text: Fantastic Greek character denied love

indicators.note: being denied something means going without it, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: the last letter of the Greek alphabet
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A wonderful Greek person turned down in romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of the Greek character is the love that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal slang for excellent or terrific, the same as fantastic used as praise.

clue.text: Bug crime boss about missing ship

indicators.note: about suggests letters moved around and scattered into a new order
missing means lacking, so the letters named are left out

parts.note: taken as written
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone plants a listening device on a mafia boss who has missed the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' suggests spying on a gangster; here it is a germ.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug is informal for a germ or microorganism, which is what a microbe is.

clue.text: German knight leaving ornamental gardens to get shopping

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for German

indicators.note: something leaving a place is no longer in it, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: rockeries are garden features of rocks and plants
K is an abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A German knight leaves the formal gardens to go to the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: A rockery is a British garden bed built of stones with alpine plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Groceries are the food and household goods bought at a shop, so they are one's shopping.

clue.text: Smoke joint with Mark in Henry's place

indicators.note: taking someone's place means swapping in for them, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: the shoulder is a joint of the body
M is an abbreviation for mark
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone lights a cannabis joint in the company of Mark, who stands where Henry used to.
explanation.walkthrough: The M goes where the H was in the body joint, turning SHOULDER into SMOULDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoulder is to burn slowly with smoke and no flame, so it is a verb for giving off smoke.

clue.text: Relative curtailed turn around block? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: curtailed literally means having the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: A relative is cut short in the middle of turning around a city block.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the reverse of 'block': the opposite of blocking a drain is clearing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclog is to free a blocked pipe or passage, the exact opposite of blocking it.

clue.text: Can't stand articles on blog, essentially

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the articles are placed second
the essence of something is its core, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the two letters at the heart of the word
the indefinite and definite articles, A and THE

explanation.surface: A grumble about the pieces posted on a blog, which the writer cannot bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests blog posts, but it means the grammatical articles.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to detest strongly; saying you can't stand something expresses the same intense dislike.

clue.text: Setter's right to be vulgar

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I, so setter's is I'M, short for I am
right and proper, as in correct or fitting

explanation.surface: The setter claims the right to be crude.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'the setter' is the author speaking of themselves, so 'Setter's' becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means indecent or in bad taste, which is what vulgar describes.

clue.text: Outlaw gang stripped city

parts.note: a band is a group or gang of people

indicators.note: stripping removes the outer covering, so the first and last letters are taken off

parts.note: what remains when the outer letters are removed

explanation.surface: A criminal gang has looted a city bare.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber living outside the law, so the noun is a synonym of outlaw.

clue.text: One who flies a criminal to Saturn?

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether a lawbreaker flies off to Saturn, as if escaping to space.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'One who flies' is loose: this flier travels in space, not by plane.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is a person trained to travel in a spacecraft, so is someone who flies, beyond the atmosphere.

clue.text: Fabulous creature looked at drunk

parts.note: a troll is a creature of fables and folk tales
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A mythical being gazed at someone who was inebriated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' here means from fable, not wonderful. Trolleyed is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Trolleyed is informal British slang meaning heavily intoxicated, one of many jokey words for drunk.

clue.text: Wife, having beaten conviction, exposed false statement

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
hit, as a past participle, means beaten or struck

indicators.note: something exposed has had its covering removed, so the outer letters are dropped

parts.note: the word belief, a conviction, with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A wife who escaped a criminal conviction is revealed to have lied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conviction' suggests a court verdict, but here it means a firm belief, which is then stripped of its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A white lie is a harmless untruth told out of tact, a kind of false statement.

clue.text: Workers putting squeeze on national party in deadlock

indicators.note: squeezing something is gripping it from both sides, so one part is held inside another

parts.note: the staff are the workers of an organisation
N is an abbreviation for national
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Employees pressure a national political party during a stalemate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics but is a social do; the pair of short pieces goes inside the workers, after their third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a situation where neither side can advance, the same thing as a deadlock.

clue.text: Candidate one trained to catch quarry

indicators.note: catching something means holding it, so another piece sits inside
something trained has been shaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a quarry is a pit dug for stone, like a mine

explanation.surface: A contender, schooled to bring down a hunted animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarry' suggests prey being hunted, but it is a stone pit; the rearranged word wraps it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone put forward for an election or award, so a candidate.

clue.text: Nazi paramilitaries wearing swords petrified masses

indicators.note: something worn is put on around the wearer, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: foils are fencing swords
the SS was the Nazi party's paramilitary organisation

explanation.surface: Armed Nazi troops terrified crowds of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petrified' reads as terrified, but here it means turned to stone, and 'masses' are lumps, not crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: Fossils are the remains of ancient life turned to stone, so they are lumps of matter petrified over time.

clue.text: Remove tariff

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cut out, as a surgeon or editor does
second meaning: a duty charged on goods

explanation.walkthrough: The two readings are pronounced differently: the verb stresses the second syllable, the tax the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Excise as a verb means to cut away, and as a noun it is a tax levied on goods, like a tariff.

clue.text: Warm shade of pink envelops outskirts of Dehli

indicators.note: an envelope wraps round its contents, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: coral is a pinkish-orange colour

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the city name, as printed

explanation.surface: A warm pink hue wraps the suburbs of the Indian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue misspells Delhi as 'Dehli', but its outer letters are the same either way; the pair goes after the colour's third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means friendly and sincere in manner, so a cordial welcome is a warm one.

clue.text: Blended rum also added to chef's latest recipes

indicators.note: blending mixes things together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the latest of a sequence is its final item, so the last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A chef's newest dishes involve rum mixed in as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A formula can be a set method or mixture of ingredients, so formulas are recipes in a broad sense.

clue.text: Withered leg confines king

indicators.note: to confine is to shut something in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the shank is the lower part of the leg
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A wasted, shrivelled leg keeps a monarch hobbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrank, the past tense of shrink, means shrivelled up or grew smaller, as something withered does.

clue.text: Appropriate dimensions to conserve energy

indicators.note: conserving something means keeping it safe inside, so one letter sits within

parts.note: the dimensions of something are its size
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Fitting measurements are needed to save power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as the adjective meaning suitable, but it is the verb meaning to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take something for oneself, often without permission, which is to seize it.

clue.text: Illustrious day school making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way one came, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: D is an abbreviation for day
Eton College, the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A distinguished day school is staging a revival.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is England's best-known private boarding school, a crossword stock answer for 'school'.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known and respected, so a noted figure is an illustrious one.

clue.text: Sprightly bird circling north in Utah

indicators.note: circling something means going all the way round it, so the bird's letters wrap the rest

parts.note: the jay is a bird of the crow family

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so a letter goes into the state

parts.note: UT is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Utah
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A lively bird flies in loops over the northern part of Utah.
explanation.walkthrough: The N sits inside UT, and that group sits inside the bird, between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaunty means lively and self-confident in manner, a near synonym of sprightly.

clue.text: Home that is filled with junk captivating international pioneer

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: something filled with stuff holds it inside, so the next piece sits within

parts.note: i.e., the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

indicators.note: to captivate is literally to take captive, so a letter is held inside

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless rubbish
I is an abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A house full of rubbish has captured a world-class trailblazer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pioneer' looks like a noun but works as the verb. Tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate is to start or set something going, which is what pioneering a scheme means.

clue.text: Remain without a drug for common complaint

indicators.note: being without something means lacking it, so that letter is left out

parts.note: to stay is to remain
taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Holding out without drugs to treat an everyday ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small, painful swelling on the eyelid, an ordinary and frequent ailment.

clue.text: Banished detective put letters in order

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector in the British police
to spell a word is to set its letters in sequence

explanation.surface: An investigator has sorted out the correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' tempts as post to be filed, but putting letters in order is spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away fears or doubts, so dispelled means banished.
